original_procedure: A flame-dried 1 L flask charged with K3PO4 (anhydrous) is cooled under nitrogen, then 5-bromopyrimidine, 3-furanylboronic acid, and NiCl2(PCy3)2 are added. After equiping a reflux condenser and performing three N2 evacuate/backfill cycles, t-AmOH (210 mL) is cannula-added under argon to give a reddish mixture. The reaction is stirred at 23 °C for 1 h under positive N2 pressure, then heated at 120 °C for 1 h. The mixture is worked up by dilution with water and diethyl ether, aqueous base and brine washes, drying (Na2SO4), filtration through Celite, and concentration. The residue is recrystallized from hot hexanes (80 °C), cooled to −20 °C to give product as light tan crystals; a second recrystallization of the mother liquor provides additional product.
